statement:
Let \(a, b \geq 2\) be relatively prime integers. Let \(S\) be the set of lattice points strictly inside the triangle with vertices \((0,0)\), \((a,0)\), \((0,b)\). Determine, with proof,
\[\sum_{(x,y) \in S} (a - 2x)(b - 2y)\]
in terms of \(a\) and \(b\).

There are \(n\) types of coins with distinct positive integer denominations \(d_1, \ldots, d_n\) cents. Call a positive integer \(D\) lucky if for every positive integer \(k\), any collection of coins worth exactly \(kD\) cents can be split into \(k\) groups each worth \(D\) cents. Does a lucky number necessarily exist?

Turbo the snail plays a game on a \(2n \times 2n\) board. There are \(2n^2\) monsters that occupy \(2n^2\) distinct cells (with Turbo's knowledge). Turbo then chooses any cell, labels it \(1\), and walks through all other \(4n^2 - 1\) cells exactly once (moving to adjacent cells), labelling them \(2, 3, \ldots, 4n^2\). The score is the sum of labels on cells with monsters. Monsters try to maximize the score; Turbo tries to minimize it. Find, in terms of \(n\), the largest score the monsters can guarantee.

A sphere with center \(I\) is inscribed in tetrahedron \(ABCD\), with all dihedral angles of \(ABCD\) acute. Suppose that
\[\frac{\mathrm{vol}(IABC)}{BC} = \frac{\mathrm{vol}(IACD)}{CD} = \frac{\mathrm{vol}(IADB)}{DB}.\]
Show that \(AI\) is perpendicular to the plane \(BCD\).

For each \(n \geq 1\), determine the maximum integer \(c_n\) for which there exists a polynomial \(f\) of degree \(n\) with rational coefficients, an irrational number \(a\), and \(c_n\) distinct rational numbers \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{c_n}\) such that \(f(a + a_i)\) is rational for all \(1 \leq i \leq c_n\).
